craft_claim: Aesthetic/psychical distance produces the objective reception detached prose seeks, but distance has an antinomy: past a threshold it collapses the viewer's personal relation to the object.

supporting_evidence.location: Part II, sections 2-3 ('The antinomy of Distance'; 'The variability of Distance'), pp. 87-118
supporting_evidence.note: Bullough argues aesthetic experience depends on distance from the practical self, permitting attention to objective features, while naming an antinomy: too little distance is sentimental, too much leaves the object cold and unpersuasive.

Construal Level Theory generalizes the finding that greater psychological distance yields more abstract, higher-level construal, providing a general-psychology basis for the distance-to-abstraction tradeoff.

counterevidence.note: Section B 'Honest limit' and section H record that no study located measures an optimal distance ratio or the threshold at which the viewer's personal relation collapses, so the antinomy's collapse half is a theoretical postulate rather than a measured finding.

scope: Aesthetic reception and narratorial stance in prose.
exceptions: Deliberate Brechtian alienation, which wants the disengaging effect for political purposes.
